title: Conversational brain model A/B through the real obey-voice brain seam

post_hoc.READ_FIRST: Hand-added on 2026-08-30, after the run, during PR #71 review. Every other key in this file is harness output; this one is not. It records two things the run knew and the artifact did not.

concurrent_load.observed: A live obey-voice session — an interactive process plus its own qwen3-tts-worker — was seen running on this machine from about 18:27 to 18:32 local, alongside a long-running VM. The observation was made at run time and written only into the report prose. Samples carry no wall clock, so from this file alone the window cannot be attributed to individual samples; it has to be reconstructed.
concurrent_load.reconstruction_method: generated_at (18:26:34-06:00) is stamped before the first model runs, so it is the run's start, not its end. The run is strictly serialized. Summing cold_first_turn.total_ms with every sample total_ms gives 219.5s for the qwen3:30b block and 203.6s for qwen3.8-uncensored:27b's — excluding warm-ups, unloads and router calls, so both are lower bounds. The incumbent is re-warmed last and was left resident under keep_alive 10m with a recorded expiry of 18:44:23, which places the run's final request at ~18:34:23 and its total length at ~7.8 minutes.
concurrent_load.coverage: The observed window covers roughly 5 of those ~7.8 minutes: effectively the whole qwen3:30b block and the front of the incumbent's. Both headline speak_ttft_p50_ms figures are inside it (4096.659 empty and 7024.136 at 6k for qwen3:30b), as is the incumbent's empty_history block (2244.357). The medians are inside the window, not only the tails.
concurrent_load.independent_corroboration: qwen3.8:latest — a model this run never measured, and the model every persona profile pins — appears in this file's notes as left resident with an expiry of 18:41:39, i.e. last used around 18:31:39 under the same 10m keep_alive. Not by this benchmark, which only ever re-warms qwen3.8-uncensored:27b.
concurrent_load.what_survives: The structural finding, which is arithmetic over committed fields rather than a clock. qwen3:30b emits a reasoning prologue of ~1.5-2.9k characters before its first spoken word and the incumbent emits none (think_chars_median 1551 and 2862 against 0 and 0). Dividing think_chars by four characters per token and by gen_tok_s predicts median waits of 4.6s and 8.0s against the measured 4.1s and 7.0s — within about 15%, erring high. The wait a listener hears on qwen3:30b is think-generation-bound, and machine load does not create that.
concurrent_load.what_is_soft: Every quantitative claim: the 1.8x and 3.0x spoken-word ratios, both medians, both tails, and the 5.5x/4.4x raw first-token ratios. Load depresses generation rate, and a depressed rate moves the measured wait and the reconstruction above together, so their agreement is not a clean bill of health. Do not read the medians as safe — an earlier version of the report did, and that reading is withdrawn. Firming any of these numbers requires a re-run on a quiet machine.
concurrent_load.not_affected: The behavioural findings: zero think leaks across 60 turns, and the incumbent's four unprompted run_command calls. Neither is a timing measurement.

projection.issue: speak_ttft_ms was measured with a harness-local copy of the pipeline's speech path. It applied ChunkSentencesRaw, one per-turn ThinkFilter and CleanForVoice, but not the voice gate, not the pronounceable half of the speakability predicate, and not the turn's repeat suppression. A reply opening on tool output or a fenced block could therefore have been timed as a spoken word that production suppresses (PR #71 review, veronica-agent).
projection.fix: The harness now calls pipeline.SpeechProjection — the same code the turn loop runs, not a copy of it. Regression coverage for a gate-suppressed leading segment is in pkg/voiceagent/pipeline/speech_projection_test.go.
projection.effect_on_this_dataset: All 60 committed replies were re-segmented and replayed through the complete projection. The first spoken segment is identical in 60 of 60, so no timing figure in this artifact or its report moves. Across 1157 segments the voice gate suppresses 0 lines, and exactly 2 segments change admission — both in qwen3.8-uncensored:27b / empty_history / P4 rep 3, where the model emitted its reply, then a stray </think>, then the identical reply again. Production's turn-scoped repeat suppression speaks that once; the harness copy had none, so that sample's spoken field carries the reply twice.
projection.spoken_chars: spoken and spoken_chars in this file are ThinkFilter output — before CleanForVoice and before gating — so they count markdown the listener never hears and run slightly high. Recomputed through the complete projection the per-condition medians are 163 / 132 / 221 / 337 characters against the committed 162 / 132 / 220 / 335, and every discard percentage in the report is unchanged. Runs after 2026-08-30 record the post-gate, post-cleaning text and a gate_suppressed_lines count.
projection.regeneration: Deliberately not regenerated. Re-running the models produces a fresh sample of a noisy machine rather than a corrected version of this one, and the replay above shows the correction changes no number in it. The honest repair for this artifact is the annotation; the honest repair for the number is a quiet-machine re-run.

config_layering.note: config brain_provider is grok, but every persona profile pins provider ollama, so the persona overlay decides. The ollama path is what the live session logs show, and it is what is measured here.

system_prompt.elements: persona + environment + skills catalog + turn instruction (brain.AssembleSystemPrompt, ollama policy)

gate.g5: G1-G4 must hold in both history conditions
gate.p95_caveat: nearest-rank on n=15; read as worst observed, not a distributional claim

prompts.text: In one sentence, tell me what you're good at.
Explain briefly what a vector database is.
I've got two hours before a meeting and three tasks: prep slides, review a pull request, and reply to email. How should I order them, and why?
Should I use a local model or a cloud model for voice? Keep it short.

filled_history.source: scripts/brain_bench/history.go — real dialogue about this repository's work, tail-trimmed to fit

notes: Latency only. Nothing here judges response quality; that is the user's judgment in real use.
Each sample resets history to the condition baseline first, so prompt size is constant across reps.
route_ms is the synchronous skill-router embedding call and is included in ttft_ms, because the user waits for it.

ttft_ms stops on the first streamed token; speak_ttft_ms stops on the first segment that survives the pipeline's ThinkFilter and voice cleaning. On a reasoning model the gap between them is the reasoning prologue, which nobody hears.
~/.obey was read, never written. No model was pulled or deleted. Models were unloaded (not removed) to measure cold load.
